assumptions: The fragments are joined in the order given, the first being the backbone.
Each method's arm is its own authority's number, stated per primer (Novagen TB163, EMBL PEPcore, Takara, the CPEC protocol sheet).
Melting temperatures are the stated nearest-neighbour model's at the stated conditions.
limits: USER designs CONSECUTIVE junctions only, as its own designer does: there is no wrap from the last fragment back to the first, because a circular USER construct closes on the vector's own fixed 3' extensions (Bitinaite et al. use pNEB206A's 8 nt), which this does not design.

USER's extension is found, not chosen, so `arm_nt` does not apply to it: the dU has to land on a dT and the two tails at a junction have to be each other's reverse complement. Each junction's extension is reported in `extensions`.

A USER chain whose junction has no A-to-T pair inside 6–10 nt is refused by name rather than designed around: the upstream search then tails one primer twice, giving two uracils and a nicked molecule that cannot anneal.
Does not screen the primers for dimers, hairpins or off-target priming; check them separately.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which primers amplify each fragment with the arm that makes a junction this method's chemistry can close, and is that arm one its own authority stands behind?

description: Design the PCR primers a ligation-independent reaction needs — LIC, SLIC, In-Fusion, CPEC or USER: a Tm-matched pair per amplified fragment, in the order given.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

arm_nt.description: the homology arm on ONE primer, which is the unit every one of these authorities states. Left unset, the method's own recommended arm. Does not apply to USER, which finds its extension instead. In nt.

backbone.description: whether the first fragment is amplified with the others (pydna splits each junction across the two neighbouring primers, so the junction is twice the arm) or supplied already cut (the whole arm goes on its neighbour's primer, and the junction is the arm). Values: amplified (Amplified), linearized (Linearized).

circular.description: close the ring: the last fragment also overlaps the first. USER does not wrap on its own, so a USER ring needs a vector named below.

conditions.description: salt, magnesium, dNTP and oligo concentrations plus the salt-correction method the target Tm is measured in. Left unset it is filled from your reaction-conditions settings, and falls back to pydna's Taq defaults when there are none. Advanced.

additives.description: DMSO and formamide, applied AFTER the nearest-neighbour Tm.

DMSOfactor.description: °C of Tm lost per % DMSO, as an explicit override. Supplying it WINS over `dmsoMethod`, and detaches the number from its citation.

dmsoMethod.description: which published DMSO depression sets the coefficient. Values: ahs01 (Ahsen et al. (2001) (0.75 °C per %)), mus81 (Musielski et al. (1981) (0.6 °C per %)), cul76 (Cullen and Bick (1976) (0.5 °C per %)), esc80 (Escara and Hutton (1980) (0.675 °C per %)).

fmd.description: formamide — percent when `fmdmethod` is 1, molar when it is 2.

fmdfactor.description: °C lost per % formamide (method 1). Papers report 0.6 to 0.72.

fmdmethod.description: 1 = linear % formamide (McConaughy 1969) · 2 = GC-dependent, molar (Blake & Delcourt 1996). Values: 1 (Linear %, McConaughy 1969), 2 (GC-dependent molar, Blake & Delcourt 1996).

method.description: which validated nearest-neighbour model and default buffer — santaLucia (pydna `tm_default`, Taq) or dbd (pydna `tm_dbd`, Phusion / Pfu-Sso7d). Values: santaLucia (SantaLucia (pydna tm_default, Taq)), dbd (DNA-binding domain (pydna tm_dbd, Phusion)).

nnTable.description: override the method's nearest-neighbour table; the buffer convention is unchanged.

saltcorr.description: Biopython salt-correction method 0–7 (0 = none). It moves the answer more than any other knob here: on a 24-mer at the Taq buffer the eight span 79.302 °C (method 0) to 66.009 °C (method 2).

selfcomp.description: both strands are one self-complementary oligo (the concentration term becomes dnac1 rather than dnac1 − dnac2/2).

eklic.description: LIC only: use the Ek/LIC vectors' own fixed extensions (Novagen TB163) instead of designing an arm. One insert only, and the vector is supplied cut.

eklic_tag.description: Ek/LIC only: keep the C-terminal tag, or close the insert with the in-frame stop TB163 gives for a construct that omits it. Advanced.

fragments.description: the fragments to join, IN ASSEMBLY ORDER, the first being the backbone — wire upstream `record` outputs here, or name library documents.

include_subject.description: put the node's subject first, as the backbone.

method.description: the cloning method, which decides what the tail is: LIC's arm is the Ek/LIC vectors' fixed overhang, SLIC's and CPEC's are ranges, In-Fusion widens its own for more than one insert, and USER's is a complementary dU pair whose length the search finds. Values: lic (LIC), slic (SLIC), in-fusion (In-Fusion), cpec (CPEC), user (USER).

min_footprint.description: shortest annealing footprint the designer may settle for (pydna's `limit`). In nt. Advanced.

target_tm.description: target annealing Tm for each primer's 3' footprint. In °C.

user_vector.description: USER only: join the two outer ends to a vector that already carries fixed 3' extensions, which is how a USER construct closes a ring. pNEB206A is the vector the method's own paper uses. Values: none (None (linear chain)), pNEB206A (pNEB206A).

user_vector_end.description: USER with a vector: which of its two DIFFERENT extensions the first fragment's forward primer matches, which is what sets the insert's orientation in the vector. Values: left (Left (GGAGACAU)), right (Right (GGGAAAGU)). Advanced.

name: design_ligation_independent_primers

armVerdict.description: whether that arm is one the method's authority stands behind, in its own words

extensions.description: USER only: per junction, the two fragments it joins, the single-stranded 3' extension each side gets (which is also where the dU sits), both tails, and whether that length is one the authority stands behind

junctionBp.description: the homology the design creates at each junction — the number `ligation_independent_clone.arm_nt` needs for the reaction to be predicted as designed

primerCount.description: oligos to order (two per amplified fragment)

primers.description: per amplified fragment: the tailed amplicon its primers make, that amplicon's length, and both primers with tail, footprint, length and footprint Tm

reactants.description: the molecules that actually react, as sequence RECORDS: the amplicons where primers were designed, and any fragment supplied cut as itself. THIS is what to wire into `ligation_independent_clone.fragments`, not the untailed fragments

summary.description: what was designed, naming the method and its chemistry

vectorEnds.description: USER with a vector: the two FIXED extensions that close the ring, which tail went on which outer primer, and where they come from. Not designed, because the vector was manufactured with them. Null when no vector is named, since a linear chain has no fixed ends to close on
